title: Pentaryn Movement
description: Players' own tokens draw on top for them (client-side: their tokens take the click when tokens overlap; nothing is written to the scene). A ghost button in the token tools lets a player move their own tokens through walls and creatures, reusing core's unconstrained-movement constrain options (ignoreWalls, ignoreCost, and dnd5e's ignoreTokens); their tokens look see-through while it is on. The GM governs it with a world setting (Off / Exploration only / Always allowed; Exploration only switches it off while a combat is running on the scene) and a toolbar button that flips it off and back. An incorporeal creature (a feat named Incorporeal Passage / Movement or Ethereal, or the GM's Token HUD toggle) keeps ghosting during a fight. Dragging a token past a wall finds the shortest way around it (A* on the grid, through open doors only, around blocking creatures and costlier terrain, a large token only where it fits; players route only around walls they have seen) with rounded corners where an arc costs no extra movement; a world setting (Everyone / GM only / Off) and two client settings govern it. Several tokens dragged together each walk their own route to their own spot, started in turn so they file through doors without overlapping (straight lines with ghost or the GM's unconstrained tool); clicking a moving token stops it on the nearest free square (in a fight, at the next square, so the movement spent stays exact); a click on one member stops the whole group (only the clicker's own members when it does not own them all). A GM toolbar button turns the drag help off for the table. Exposes game.pentaryn.movement.

afterSync: First install: restart Foundry (module.json is read at startup), enable 'Pentaryn Movement', then reload.
Players get a Ghost toggle in the token tools; the GM sets the policy in settings.
